processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The ingot was reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
The ingot was forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm; the starting forging temperature was 1100 °C and the finishing forging temperature was 950 °C.
After forging, the bars were cooled to RT in the furnace.

Tensile test carried out on a YYF-50 tensile tester until fracture at -196 °C with liquid nitrogen as cooling medium; strain rate 0.001 s-1 (10-3 s-1), slow enough to avoid frictional heat; extensometer used; parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1.5 mm; three tensile samples tested per condition for average values.

structures.overall_structure: Deformed austenite (uniform deformation section) after tensile deformation at -196 °C: fully austenitic (no DIMT), crystal orientation concentrated in {111} and {001}, dominated by planar glide of dislocations with a small amount of mechanical twins; LAGB fraction 70.2%, HAGB fraction 29.8%; GNDs accumulate at LAGBs.

microstructure_list.region: uniformly deformed section (~10 mm from the fracture surface, not affected by necking)

phases_present.morphology: deformed equiaxed austenite grains with crystal orientation concentrated in {111} and {001}

defects.type: low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) with GND accumulation
defects.lattice_distortion: GNDs accumulate at LAGBs indicating more severe local deformation

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: LAGBs mainly concentrate at the austenite grains with finer grain size

phases_present.morphology: dark parallel band-like features (mechanical twins) in a heavily dislocated matrix

defects.type: mechanical twins (twinning plane along <112> on {111}, grain oriented near <110> zone axis)

phase_interfaces.coherence: mechanical twinning plane formed along <112> crystal direction on {111} plane

defect_interactions.interaction_type: GND accumulation at low-angle grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: GNDs accumulate at LAGBs, indicating a more severe local deformation of these regions.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: product of planar glide (mechanical twins/microbands) acting as barriers to partial dislocation motion
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Mechanical twins and glide bands act as barriers for the movement of partial dislocations, contributing to a high work hardening rate at -196 °C.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar glide of dislocations dominates; the reduced SFE at -196 °C (32 mJ/m²) promotes planar glide and hampers cross-slip, with a small amount of mechanical twinning formed; twinning plane {111} along <112> in grains oriented near <110> zone axis.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Austenite remains fully stable with no deformation-induced martensitic transformation (DIMT); no isothermal martensite forms at -196 °C; only mechanical twinning occurs in addition to planar glide.

measurement_conditions.environment: liquid nitrogen (used as cooling medium; entire tensile process carried out in cooling medium)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: parallel length 32 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1.5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: YYF-50 tensile tester until fracture; extensometer used; three samples tested per condition to obtain average values; microstructure analyzed on the uniformly deformed section ~10 mm from the fracture

elongation.value: > 65 % (total elongation; largest strain of the three temperatures)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve at -196 °C (Fig. 2a); corresponding true stress-strain curve and work hardening rate curve (Fig. 2b); the necking point corresponds to σtrue = dσtrue/dεtrue.
strain_hardening_rate: Work hardening rate increases as deformation temperature decreases (negative temperature dependence of strength).

density.value: 7.114 g/cm3 (measured); 7.078 g/cm3 (estimated by Kim et al. equation)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Decreasing tensile temperature to -196 °C (reduced SFE, 32 mJ/m²) raises glide planarity, giving higher tensile strength and elongation than at -77 °C and RT (negative temperature dependence of strength and a higher work hardening rate).

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) - IPF, grain boundary (GB) and GND/kernel average misorientation maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac scanning electron microscope (SEM)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: step size 0.5 μm; analyzed on the uniformly deformed section ~10 mm from the fracture after mechanical polishing to remove the deformation layer
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze the tensile deformed microstructure (crystal orientation, boundary fractions, GND distribution)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Crystal orientation concentrated in {111} and {001}; LAGB fraction 70.2% and HAGB fraction 29.8% at -196 °C; a small amount of mechanical twins marked with arrows; GNDs accumulate at LAGBs

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tecnai F30 field emission TEM; specimens double-jet thinned using a Struers TenuPol-5 Twin-Jet Electropolisher (electrolyte 6% perchloric acid + 94% glacial acetic acid)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SAED recorded along zone axis Z.A. [1,1,0]
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the mechanical twins and dislocations in the -196 °C tensile-deformed microstructure
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dark parallel band-like features identified as mechanical twins in a heavily dislocated matrix; twinning plane along <112> on {111} in grains oriented near <110> zone axis; SAED reflections (1,-1,1), (0,0,2), (0,0,-2), (1,-1,-1) consistent with twin-related reflections

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: -196 °C in liquid nitrogen; strain rate 0.001 s-1; three samples per condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: Highest strength and elongation at -196 °C; work hardening rate highest at the lowest temperature

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of the tensile fracture surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the fracture surface after tensile tests

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic/analytical estimation of stacking fault energy (SFE)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Input lattice parameter of austenite (0.36757 nm) determined from XRD analysis

analytical_models.equation_role: SFE = 2 ρ_A ΔG^{γ→ε} + 2 σ^{γ/ε}, with σ^{γ/ε} taken as 15 mJ/m²; ρ_A from ρ_A = (4/√3)·(1/(N·α_γ²)); ΔG^{γ→ε} from the summation over alloying-element free energies, interaction energies, X_C ΔG_{FeMnAl/C}^{γ→ε} and the magnetic free-energy term
analytical_models.model_note: Estimated SFE of the experimental steel is 32 mJ/m² at -196 °C (40 mJ/m² at -77 °C and 61 mJ/m² at RT).

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical work-hardening analysis (Hollomon equation, two-stage fit)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Applied to the measured true stress-strain curves at -196 °C (Fig. 8)

analytical_models.equation_role: σ = K ε^n; linearized as lnσ = lnK + n·lnε to obtain the work hardening exponents
analytical_models.model_note: Work hardening behavior divided into two stages; exponents increase as temperature decreases.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel at -196 °C is estimated to be 32 mJ/m², which still totally suppresses DIMT but enables the occurrence of mechanical twinning; mechanical twinning is reported as the main deformation mechanism for high-Mn steels when SFE is between 18 and 35 mJ/m².
Two-stage work-hardening exponents at -196 °C from the Hollomon analysis: n1 = 0.204 (low-strain region) and n2 = 0.448 (high-strain region), the largest of the three tensile temperatures.
Reported linear temperature dependence of tensile strength (T in °C): UTS = 813.0 - 2.36×T and YS = 474.6 - 2.05×T (Fig. 2c); both YS and UTS increase linearly as deformation temperature decreases.
At -196 °C the tensile necking point (where true stress equals the work hardening rate, σtrue = dσtrue/dεtrue) occurs at the highest stress and true strain among the three temperatures.

The region flanking the primary crack is transgranular: misorientation analysis across the crack (Fig. 10c) shows a misorientation difference of less than 15° between the regions on both sides of the crack, i.e., they belonged to the same grain before cracking.
